title: Aspartame and cancer - new evidence for causation.
ehr_evidence: RI subjected all HLTs from aspartame-exposed animals to immunohistochemical analysis using a battery of markers and to morphological reassessment using the most recent Internationally Harmonized Nomenclature and Diagnostic (INHAND) criteria.
summary: Commentary re-evaluating Ramazzini Institute rodent toxicology studies, confirming aspartame-induced hematolymphatic malignancies and prenatal carcinogenic effects through immunohistochemical and morphological reassessment.
key_findings: Immunohistochemical and morphological re-evaluation confirmed malignancy in 92.3% of originally diagnosed hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue tumors.
Six lesions originally diagnosed as lymphoma were reclassified: 3 to lymphoid hyperplasia and 3 to chronic inflammation with fibrosis.
No histological evidence of Mycoplasma pulmonis infection was found.
Statistically significant increase in incidence of all hematolymphatic malignancies (p = 0.006), including lymphomas (p = 0.032) and leukemias (p = 0.031).
Positive dose-response relationship observed between aspartame exposure and hematolymphatic malignancy incidence.
Prenatal exposures produced dose-related increases in malignancies at lower exposure levels and shorter latency than adult exposures.
captured_features: immunohistochemical markers (Ki67, CD3, PAX5, CD20, CD68, TdT, CD45, CD14, CD33)
hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue tumor diagnoses
limitations: re-evaluation based on existing rodent bioassay data
extrapolation of rodent findings to human health risks
